title: Hippocampus KI living-memory architecture
desc: Neuro-named map of the hongik harness two-stage memory: hippocampus (real-time encoding via auto-topic-MD), recall (wkfind/session-find retrieval over session JSONL), sleep consolidation (skill-heal-nightly). Single findable entry point tying the scattered memory-vision pieces together.
steps: REFLEX TRAJECTORY (wkhippo reflex, every family): WHEN, HOW, HOW MUCH. THE PRINCIPLE (owner 2026-10-12): a program is studied and debugged by the trace of the functions it executed; an intelligence is studied and debugged by the trajectory of the reflexes it executed, so read the trajectory before its report, its letter or its source (example 2026-10-13: docs root cf10a0b4 rewrote a gg report five times while its rows held three measuring sectors and zero submit calls); the trajectory shows the forest without pushing raw transcript noise into context, so you pick the exact spot and attack only there (owner 2026-10-12: a new law of the AI world; example: the user rows of seat 1bab4336 showed in one grep the one open owner order that had no root). (1) SEAT START or after compaction: wkhippo reflex --all --cwd REPO --since 24h --rows once, to find the predecessor seat, take over the owner's last orders from its user rows and learn from its blocked rows. (2) PATROL every inbox sweep, and before trusting any root's report: wkhippo reflex --all --cwd REPO --since 60m --summary per commanded repo, never split by --family; open --rows only on a root whose summary shows many reads with few edits or one refusal tag repeating. (3) ONE SESSION: wkhippo reflex SID-PREFIX --rows --since 30m, add --keep WORD to narrow; raw JSON (no flag) only when you need a tool argument. HOW MUCH: summary first, rows only for the window you will act on, never the default raw dump of a whole day; the ONE exception is a new spokesman seat, which reads its predecessor seat over its WHOLE life (wkhippo reflex SEAT --rows --since 48h, every user row), because a tail window hides the owner orders still open (owner 2026-10-12: partial reading is a failed initialization). Example: 2026-10-11 a summary showed codex roots at 300 reads, 2 edits and 10 hook-deadline refusals an hour, a gate defect found without reading one row. Recent-activity text search stays wkhippo recent KEYWORD. //why:kih root rows opened only after stop loop suspicion //why:predecessor seat user rows showed three open owner orders-haiku //why:SDK codex root spent 5.6M input tokens and landed nothing-haiku //why:kih root rows opened only after stop loop suspicion-opus

RECALL BECOMES FORESIGHT (the core principle): before choosing an approach, recall whether a PREDECESSOR session already tried it and how it turned out, then infer your future from that senior outcome instead of repeating the wrong road. The session corpus is a predecessor-mistake oracle: consult BEFORE acting, not after failing. This covers tool flags as well: before you trust a launcher flag, grep its source or recall it. Example: wkroot -model sonnet on a fresh launch is drawn by lottery (owner policy 2026-10-02), so it is not a bug. //why:kih sonnet root rows checked before resending codex brief //why:predecessor recall preceded the guard fix choice-haiku //why:success roads should outnumber blocked rows over weeks-opus //why:kih sonnet root rows checked before resending codex brief-opus

METAPHOR: the hongik harness memory mirrors the human brain. HIPPOCAMPUS equals real-time encoding (force-capture hard facts like dates, case numbers, deadlines, citations, decisions the turn they appear, via an auto-topic-MD exporter). RECALL equals ripgrep retrieval over all-AI raw session transcripts. SLEEP CONSOLIDATION equals skill-heal-nightly (daily 04:13 Opus cron: heal skills, compact CLAUDE.md Pending, dedup). Core law: capture the moment the turn it happens, or lose it. //why:capture refused dispatch at once-sonnet //why:codex agy moments must be captured like claude-haiku //why:sector built overcome reflex rows encoding-haiku //why:stop refusal loop recorded as one healing line

WKHIPPO equals THE FINAL-FORM FRONT DOOR and the single fixed way to express every memory action. wkhippo with no args equals STATUS (announce of encoding, recall, sleep state); wkhippo recall (kw) equals recall (hoesang); wkhippo foresee (kw) equals predecessor-outcome foresight (mirae-gwancheuk); wkhippo export (sessionid) equals encoding (haema). There are NO standalone aliases: the former wkrecall and wkforesee commands were removed 2026-06-05, so every memory action is a wkhippo subcommand, for consistency and easy future discovery. Always call the wkhippo subcommand form. Read-only wk tool, kept pace and busy-fleet exempt for frictionless recall. //why:family filter needs handler to call parser

ENCODING FLOOR: at minimum one guaranteed end-of-session life-review (wkhippo export plus opus-self-reflection on session end or before compaction) so the next session is born already remembering its predecessor; rebirth equals post-compaction-recovery reading what the death-bed review saved. Per-turn encode is the ideal, one death-bed encode is the acceptable floor. //why:sector agy settings model identity inventory //why:moment inventory measurement capture //why:reflex-healing moment capture skill

NAVIGATION plus CLUSTER: usage, the wkhippo subcommands, recall spec, encoding trigger, and the wkfind four-source find organ are in wkappbot skill read hippocampus-living-memory-howto. Genesis, intent-via-subcommand, the security-audit and AGI angle, productization, and the dated build-status log are in wkappbot skill read hippocampus-living-memory-ref. CLUSTER: wkfind (find organ), wkrecall (recall alias), skill-heal-nightly (consolidation), harness-learn-self-evolving-skills (encoding design), knowledge-ification-procedure-jisikhwa (the why), post-compaction-recovery (rebirth).

HARNESS CACHE BACKEND (user 2026-06-23, architectural direction): the wkhippo indexer (SQLite global_indexer) is the canonical persistent store for ALL harness per-call caches -- the session-JSONL skill-read scan, model detection, compaction-boundary, pace state, etc. Each PreToolUse hook runs as a FRESH process, so in-memory (script-scoped) caches die every call and the hook re-scans from scratch (the sub-1s violation: a ~15MB JSONL re-parsed per tool call, worsening as the session grows). Routing every such cache through the wkhippo indexer (keyed on source path + mtime) lets a fresh hook READ the cached result instead of re-scanning. One indexer = one cache backend for the whole harness = the structural sub-1s fix. Cross: harness-gate-log-data-integrity (the perf TODO + this architecture), wk-tool-sub-1s-response-time-mandate. //why:reflex now registers sessions in the canonical indexer for every family-sonnet //why:gate reads reflex rows not raw transcripts-opus //why:gate reads reflex rows not raw transcripts-opus

PRECISE LINE TRACKING: Leveraging the binary line indexer (wk-memory-index.idx), recall results now include the exact line number of every match in the session JSONL. This allows the AI and user to jump directly to the context immediately preceding a block, satisfying the 'was the guidance appropriate' audit requirement. //why:reflex help should mention line numbers //why:reflex raw output should also carry exact line numbers //why:owner asked whether reflex prints raw jsonl lines //why:owner asked whether reflex prints raw jsonl lines-opus //why:reflex raw output should also carry exact line numbers-sonnet //why:reflex help should mention line numbers-sonnet

WHEN: the next session touching harness performance, or any session where PreToolUse exceeds its threshold and starts refusing tool calls. HOW: run wkappbot skill read hippocampus-living-memory-howto for the wkhippo subcommand surface, then give the indexer the three queries these guards actually need -- how many times a named skill was read in THIS session, the id of the LAST skill edited, and the count of delegations inside the last N minutes -- keyed on source path plus mtime, so a fresh hook process reads a cached answer instead of re-parsing; the call sites are wkharness-guards-evidence.ps1 lines 64 and 207 and wkharness-guards-agent.ps1 line 99, all in wkappbot-kih. WHY: VERIFIED ABSENT 2026-08-29 -- grepping wkharness-guards-evidence.ps1 for global_indexer, wk-memory-index and hippo returns ZERO matches, so the guards have never consulted the indexer even though tools/global_indexer.py exists in both repos. AND THE PATCH THAT LANDED TODAY DOES NOT CLOSE THIS: replacing Get-Content with ReadLines at those three sites removed the per-line PSObject allocation and cleared the block, but the read is still O(session size) and still runs on EVERY tool call, so the cost merely grows more slowly. The owner named the real fix the same day -- route session-content search through the indexer so no guard rescans a growing transcript at all, and every AI family shares one index instead of each re-deriving it. THE MEASURE THAT MAKES IT WORTH DOING: this session climbed from 4231 ms to 11109 ms against a 3000 ms threshold on a 2.5 MB transcript, and the gate blocked Bash, Write, Edit and Agent -- including the very edit that repaired it. A cache keyed on mtime turns that curve into a constant. Update this step to RESULT: when a guard reads its answer from the indexer. //why:onload gate now reads codex through reflex //why:onload gate now reads codex through reflex-opus //why:onload gate now reads codex through reflex-opus

REGEX-KEYED INDEXING: The memory organ now supports regex patterns (prefixed with 're:') as indexing keys. This enables rapid OR-search and grouped retrieval of frequently accessed block patterns (e.g., agent-brief triggers) and compliance markers. Results are cached in a relaxed-JSON metadata format for O(1) retrieval speed.

DECISION: the three transcript scans need TWO different wirings, not one shared function, and the third must NOT be cached the way the others are. WHEN: wiring the remaining guards onto the indexer, or reviewing a claim that one shared session-query function now serves them all. HOW: run wkappbot skill read hippocampus-living-memory-howto for the wkhippo surface, then treat each by SHAPE rather than by resemblance. WHY: shape one is a COUNT over the whole transcript, which is what Get-WkEvidencePriorRefCount needs and what shipped 2026-08-29 as Get-WkEvidenceRefCountInternal keyed on transcript path plus mtime. Shape two is a LAST-MATCH CAPTURE, needed by Get-WkTierGateEditedSkillIds at wkharness-guards-evidence.ps1 line 204, which walks every line keeping the final regex capture group -- it caches the same way but stores a STRING id instead of an integer. Shape three is the trap: the delegation counter at wkharness-guards-agent.ps1 line 99 counts inside a ROLLING WINDOW measured from UtcNow, so its answer changes on every call and a naive path-plus-mtime key would serve a stale count forever; it must key on the window boundary too, or cache the parsed line set and recompute the time filter each call. THE REASON THIS DISTINCTION OUTRANKS THE SPEEDUP: an undercount in any of the three makes a gate STOP REFUSING rather than misreport, which is the worst failure direction available. THE MEASURED STARTING POINT 2026-08-29: only shape one is wired -- grepping the tool folder for the new function name outside its own file returns ZERO callers, and both remaining scans still read the whole transcript on every tool call. Update this step to RESULT: when all three are wired and an adversarial suite covers them.

INCIDENT: recall is slow because it parses what it then throws away, and its real-user-turn predicate exists TWICE with the two copies DISAGREEING BY A FACTOR OF TEN. WHEN: optimizing wkhippo recall, or touching either copy of the real-user-turn logic in session-find.ps1. HOW: run wkappbot skill read wk-tool-sub-1s-response-time-mandate for the target, then grep the file for realUserIdxs before changing anything and read BOTH hits -- New-SearchBase at line 247 and Get-RealUserIndexes at line 601 -- because the fix is lazy evaluation in both and the drift must be settled by the owner rather than silently unified by whoever edits second. WHY: measured 2026-09-03. A default 7-day repo-scoped recall over 193 sessions took 3 minutes 30 seconds against a sub-1s mandate. New-SearchBase carries a header comment promising that original JSONL is never fully converted and only exchanges containing hits are, and that promise is FALSE: once a file has any hit, the realUserIdxs pre-build runs over EVERY line and calls ConvertFrom-Json on every line of type user, no matter where the hits sit. Measured on a real 56MB transcript capped at 3000 lines with 561 user-type lines, that is 307ms of pure parse for ONE file, about 59 seconds across 193 sessions in that single loop. The fix is to compute the predicate lazily and memoized, since the backward walk stops at the first real user turn and the forward walk is already capped at 60 lines, and the previous timestamp the gap test needs is reachable by the existing regex without any parse. TWO CORRECTIONS WORTH INHERITING. First, I briefed a delegate that the idiom lived in FOUR places and it grepped, came back with TWO, and was right -- I had conflated the four Get-Content sites with the two predicate sites, so verify a site count before you put it in a brief. Second, and nobody had noticed: the two copies are not twins. Line 268 tests clean.Length under 400 while line 620 tests under 4000, so recall and the markdown export classify a human turn differently on the same transcript, and this is the hand-maintained-twins-drift defect this repo already knows by name.
